patterns.usage_note: Reports someone else's desire as behavior an observer can see (弟は私のゲームを借りたがる). It attaches to the masu-stem and conjugates as a godan verb; non-past たがる usually reads as habitual, while たがっている describes a wish being shown right now. Its object is marked with を rather than が, and because it views the person from the outside it is typically avoided about a superior or about oneself.

examples.ruby: 弟[おとうと]はいつも私[わたし]のゲームを借[か]りたがる。
examples.english: My little brother is always after my games.

examples.ruby: 同僚[どうりょう]はさっきから早[はや]く帰[かえ]りたがっている。
examples.english: My coworker has been itching to head home for a while now.

examples.ruby: 父[ちち]は誰[だれ]にでも昔話[むかしばなし]をしたがります。
examples.english: My father is only too eager to tell his old stories to anyone at all.
